explanations.explanation: This neuron detects the discourse‐level “thank you” marker—i.e. the polite expression of gratitude (usually “Thanks” at the start of a message) that frames acknowledgments or courteous closings.

The feature is simply a “capitalized‐word‐prefix” detector: it spikes whenever you see the first three letters of a proper noun (e.g. Tun- in Tunisia/Tunbridge, Kun- in Kunming, Mun- in Munster, Lot- in Lotte/Lottery, etc.), marking the onset of a named entity.

This neuron fires whenever we hit the initial sub‐segment of a capitalized content word—especially the first few letters of a proper name, acronym or technical term. In effect it’s a “prefix extractor” that flags the start of key nouns (e.g. “Em–” in Emlyn/Émilion, “Press–” in Pressac, “Comm–” in COMMITTED, “Consc–” in Conscious) or abbreviations (RDB, SP, Ch, etc.).

This neuron is simply an orthographic “IG” detector—it lights up whenever the two‐letter sequence “ig” (or its caps‐ or case‐variants) appears in a token, regardless of its meaning (e.g. Yug­ra, Gonal-F, Portug­uês, iguana, tiger, wig, indigestion, Wiggins, Pattinson, kigurumi, baking, vigil, Grigor, Hodgkin, hygienist, etc.).

This neuron is essentially a word-start prefix detector: it fires on short letter sequences at the beginning of tokens (especially capitalized ones like “Pro-,” “Geo-,” “Cy-,” “X-,” “Ox-,” “Pho-,” “Py-,” “Vy-,” etc.) that commonly signal proper names, brands, technical terms or other prefixed compounds.

This neuron fires on premodifier adjectives—especially color words (Blue, White) or similar descriptors (Private, La) —when they head multi‐word proper names, titles or brands (e.g. “Blue Sky Clinic,” “White T-shirt,” “Private Investigator Nottinghamshire”). It marks the adjective at the start of a named entity.

This feature flags “title‐style” content words at the heads of segments—the capitalized, stand-alone verbs, adjectives and nouns you see in headings, post titles or product/service names (e.g. “Experimenting,” “Magic,” “Flipping,” “Transforming,” “Management,” “Looking,” “Filtering,” etc.). It’s essentially a detector for title/headline tokens.

This feature fires on the tokens that mark the start of a new titled block or list entry in scraped/metadata text—i.e. the capitalized words, abbreviations and trailing dots that introduce headings, episode titles, honorifics or names (e.g. “Tech.,” “Ep.,” “Sen.,” person names, dates, etc.). It essentially detects those structural markers that label or head each segment.

This neuron lights up on the “head” word of a named‐entity or noun–noun compound—i.e. the final, label‐bearing token (whether a proper name like Anderson/Jackson/Chandler/Brisbane/Boeing or a service/product noun like booth, broker, board, projector, etc.) that names the core category of the phrase.
